display.title: Episode 144: Saved by a Miracle, Chapter 1 (Aseres Yemei Teshuvah)
display.summary_short: Between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, Uncle Yossi explains why Tashlich is done by flowing water, and begins the story of an honest Chassid framed by a jealous enemy.
display.summary_long: Broadcast during the Ten Days of Teshuvah, with Yom Kippur falling on Shabbos. Uncle Yossi explains that teshuvah means returning to Hashem and firmly resolving never to repeat a sin, and that this is why Tashlich is said by flowing water: like a paper swept away by a river, our sins are thrown where we can never take them back. After the Hakochainik march he introduces the story, 'Through the Eyes of a Tzaddik.' An eight-year-old boy leads the Shema, and his proud father thanks Tzivos Hashem on the air. Story time: Reb Boruch, an honest Chassid trusted by the local Russian minister to supervise a lumberyard, is envied by Alex, a cruel man fired from the same yard. Alex hides twenty costly railroad logs in Reb Boruch's barn and shows them to the minister, who summons Reb Boruch to his office on Tuesday. Frightened, Reb Boruch goes to the Alter Rebbe, who only smiles and tells him to come back next Sunday. Trusting the tzaddik, Reb Boruch decides not to appear. To be continued. The show ends with news of the Great Sukkah Experience, the Shofar Gadol contest and a refuah shleimah update.
display.lesson: Real teshuvah means deciding never to go back to a sin; and when the way is unclear, trust Hashem and the guidance of a tzaddik.

date.note: On air: 'in the middle of the Aseres Yemei Teshuvah' and 'this year Yom Kippur falls on this coming Shabbos'. Yom Kippur 5745 = Shabbos 6 Oct 1984, so the Tuesday broadcast is 2 Oct 1984.

advisories.note: A Jew is falsely accused of theft and summoned by a Russian official; people who were summoned are said to have disappeared.
